title: Aeternum Agenda
subtitle: Living Archive, Core 4: Thesis
intro: Aeternum Agenda is a thesis in progress. This is its Living Archive: the research, references, experiments, failures, questions, conversations, and observations collected week by week across Core 4: Thesis. It records how the project, and the thinking behind it, develops.

Kevin Warrick is considered by many to be the world's first cyborg. He formed a symbiotic connection with a robotic hand by linking his nervous system to a computer and controlling the hand with his brain signals. Scroll through the gallery to see more of David Vintiner's images of so-called "transhumanists." David Vintiner. Photograph.
Liz Parrish claims to be the first person to successfully undergo dual gene therapy to "treat" biological aging. David Vintiner. Photograph.
Describing himself as an "eyeborg," Rob Spence installed a wireless video camera in place of his right eye. David Vintiner. Photograph.

Neil Harbisson was born with achromatism, or total colorblindness. In 2004, he had an antenna implanted into his skull that allows him to perceive colors as audible vibrations. David Vintiner. Photograph.

Moon Ribas is a cyborg dancer who has implants connected to online seismographs in her feet. She has the ability to "sense" earthquakes taking place anywhere on the planet, she claims, as they cause vibrations to course through her body. David Vintiner. Photograph.
James Young's arm is controlled by sensors that detect the minute muscle movements in his spine. David Vintiner. Photograph.
Beauty is in the engineered products. David Vintiner. Photograph.

Neurobotics, Moscow. Neurobotics manufactures made-to-order anthropomorphic robots copying the appearance of a real person, in this instance, Aleksandr Pushkin, the Russian poet and novelist. Photograph.
